title: AgentOS Linux MVP Task Plan
objective: Deliver the first executable Linux-based AgentOS slice with agentd boot/control plane, terminal-first UX, semantic capabilities, audit, diff/rollback, and recovery.
assumptions: MVP targets x86_64 Linux with hardware virtualization available but not required for the first slice.
Debian/Ubuntu is the first package-management target unless DEC-001 changes scope.
External LLM usage remains optional; the system must support local-only or stub planner mode.
Firecracker is designed into interfaces but not required for MVP completion.

waves.name: Product and Architecture Freeze
exit_criteria: Boot target and distro base are fixed.

waves.name: Bootable Control Plane
waves.purpose: Prove Linux can hand control to agentd and that agentd can survive as the minimal control process.
exit_criteria: A minimal image boots into agentd/TUI path.
agentd has structured lifecycle and health reporting.
Operator can enter an intent and receive a deterministic plan preview.

waves.name: Semantic Runtime and Audit
waves.purpose: Prevent arbitrary shell from becoming the system boundary.
exit_criteria: Semantic tool calls are typed and routed through policy.
Every effect is journaled before execution.
Crash recovery can distinguish prepared, observed, sealed, and rollback-pending effects.

waves.name: Capability, Sandbox, and Rollback
waves.purpose: Make low and medium risk side effects constrained, inspectable, and reversible.
exit_criteria: Read-only tools run under Linux sandbox constraints.
File writes use shadow/overlay diff flow.
Approval tokens bind actor, tool, resource, parameter hash, expiry, and policy version.

waves.name: MVP Workflows and Quality Gates
waves.purpose: Drive the architecture through real workflows and regression tests.
exit_criteria: At least one real service recovery workflow runs end to end.
Prompt injection, over-permission, fork bomb, and rollback tests exist.
CI produces reproducible artifacts with basic provenance metadata.
